prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val2] 政务服务 · 办理时限 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "事项名称" spans 1 col × 2 row; "办理时限（工作日）" spans 2 col × 1 row; "所需材料" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "事项名称" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 92px
  col 2: header "办理时限（工作日） › 法定" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 31px
  col 3: header "办理时限（工作日） › 承诺" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 4: header "所需材料" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 414px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare the statutory and promised processing times for each government service item, then see the materials required for that item.","reading":"Readers scan row by row: first identify the service item, then compare the two adjacent time figures (法定 vs 承诺), then read the materials list. The two time columns need to read as a pair under their shared header; the materials column is a long reference list and will wrap.","groups":["Columns 2 and 3 belong together: they are the paired 法定/承诺 values under the shared 办理时限（工作日） header and must stay adjacent for comparison.","Column 1 is the row-identification column and should remain visually separate from the time pair.","Column 4 is an independent reference list; it can be wider or narrower but should not disrupt the time comparison."],"keep_intact":["事项名称 values ideally on one line so rows remain easy to scan","法定 and 承诺 leaf headers","numeric time values 15/1, 20/5, 10/3","办理时限（工作日） group header ideally on one line","material names and their 、 separators; break at separators rather than inside terms"],"may_wrap":["所需材料 lists, which are far wider than any feasible column","事项名称 in a materials-first design","办理时限（工作日） group header if the two time columns are compressed"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [113, 80, 80, 206] · table 480×275px · row heights [36, 36, 83, 83, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [104, 66, 66, 243] · table 480×252px · row heights [60, 36, 60, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [120, 64, 64, 231] · table 480×275px · row heights [60, 36, 83, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
